title: Ezekiel Chapter 33 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 33 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 33 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 33.

questions.question: Who is told to speak to the children of their people and warn them about the sword coming upon the land?
questions.correctAnswer: Son of man
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:2 states, 'Son of man, speak to the children of thy people, and say unto them...'

questions.question: What is the watchman instructed to do when he sees the sword come upon the land?
options: Blow the trumpet and warn the people
questions.correctAnswer: Blow the trumpet and warn the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:3 says, 'If when he seeth the sword come upon the land, he blow the trumpet, and warn the people;'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33, what happens to those who hear the trumpet but do not take warning and the sword comes upon them?
options: Their blood is upon their own head
They will be punished by the watchman
questions.correctAnswer: Their blood is upon their own head
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:4 states, 'Then whosoever heareth the sound of the trumpet, and taketh not warning; if the sword come, and take him away, his blood shall be upon his own head.'

questions.question: True or False: If the watchman sees the sword come but does not blow the trumpet, he will not be held responsible for the blood of the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:6 explains that if the watchman sees the sword and does not warn, he will be held responsible for the blood of those taken by the sword.

questions.question: What role has the LORD set for the son of man in relation to the house of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: A watchman
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:7 says, 'So thou, O son of man, I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel...'

questions.question: True or False: If the son of man does not warn the wicked of their ways, and they die in their iniquity, the son of man will not be held accountable.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:8 states that if the son of man does not warn the wicked, their blood will be required at his hand.

questions.question: What happens if the son of man warns the wicked to turn from their way but they do not turn?
options: They will die in their iniquity, but the son of man has delivered his soul
They will be punished by the watchman
questions.correctAnswer: They will die in their iniquity, but the son of man has delivered his soul
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:9 explains that if the wicked do not turn after being warned, they die in their iniquity, but the son of man is delivered.

questions.question: What question do the people ask about their transgressions and sins in Ezekiel 33?
options: If we pine away in them, how should we then live?
Why must we die for them?
questions.correctAnswer: If we pine away in them, how should we then live?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:10 records the people saying, 'If our transgressions and our sins be upon us, and we pine away in them, how should we then live?'

questions.question: What does the LORD say about His pleasure in the death of the wicked?
options: He has no pleasure in the death of the wicked
He delights in the death of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: He has no pleasure in the death of the wicked
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:11 states, 'I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live.'

questions.question: True or False: The righteousness of the righteous will always deliver him in the day of his transgression.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:12 says, 'The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression.'

questions.question: What will happen to a righteous person who trusts in his own righteousness but commits iniquity?
options: He shall die for his iniquity
He shall be punished by the watchman
questions.correctAnswer: He shall die for his iniquity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:13 states that if the righteous commits iniquity, he shall die for it despite his righteousness.

questions.question: What must the wicked do to live, according to Ezekiel 33?
options: Turn from sin, do what is lawful and right
questions.correctAnswer: Turn from sin, do what is lawful and right
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:14 says if the wicked turn from their sin and do what is lawful and right, they shall live.

questions.question: What is the result if the wicked restore what they have robbed and walk in the statutes of life without committing iniquity?
options: He shall surely live and not die
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely live and not die
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:15 states that the wicked who restore the pledge and walk in statutes of life shall surely live.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 33, what comes first: the watchman blowing the trumpet or the son of man being set as a watchman?
options: The son of man being set as a watchman
questions.correctAnswer: The watchman blowing the trumpet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:3 describes the watchman blowing the trumpet before Ezekiel is set as a watchman in Ezekiel 33:7.

questions.question: True or False: The son of man is told to warn the house of Israel from the word of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:7 states that the son of man is set as a watchman to warn the house of Israel from the word of the LORD.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 33 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 33 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33:12, what happens to the righteousness of the righteous on the day he sins?
options: It will deliver him from death
questions.correctAnswer: It will not deliver him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:12 states that the righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression, meaning his past righteousness will not save him when he sins.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 33:13 say the righteous will face if he trusts in his righteousness but commits iniquity?
options: He will die for his iniquity
His righteousness will cover his sin
questions.correctAnswer: He will die for his iniquity
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains that if the righteous trusts in his own righteousness and commits iniquity, he will die for the iniquity he has committed, and his past righteousness will not be remembered.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 33:14 say will happen if the wicked turn from their sin and do what is lawful and right?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall live
questions.explanation: Verse 14 promises that if the wicked turn from their sin and do that which is lawful and right, they shall live, emphasizing God's willingness to forgive.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33:15, which of the following actions can cause the wicked to surely live?
options: Restoring the pledge and walking in statutes without iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: Restoring the pledge and walking in statutes without iniquity
questions.explanation: Verse 15 highlights that if the wicked restore what they robbed, give again, walk in the statutes of life, and commit no iniquity, they shall surely live and not die.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 33:16 say about the sins of one who does what is lawful and right?
options: His sins will be remembered forever
His sins will be mentioned to him constantly
None of his sins will be mentioned to him
He will be punished for previous sins
questions.correctAnswer: None of his sins will be mentioned to him
questions.explanation: Verse 16 assures that none of the sins committed by a person who chooses to do what is lawful and right shall be mentioned to him, showing forgiveness and restoration.

questions.question: How do the children of Israel view the way of the Lord, according to Ezekiel 33:17?
options: They say it is just and fair
They say it is not equal
questions.correctAnswer: They say it is not equal
questions.explanation: Verse 17 records that the children of Israel say the way of the Lord is not equal, reflecting their misunderstanding of God's justice.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 33:18 say will happen when the righteous turn from righteousness and commit iniquity?
options: They will be rewarded for past deeds
questions.correctAnswer: They shall even die thereby
questions.explanation: Verse 18 clearly states that if the righteous turn from his righteousness and commit iniquity, he shall die because of that iniquity.

questions.question: What promise does Ezekiel 33:19 give to the wicked who turn from their wickedness and do what is lawful and right?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall live
questions.explanation: Verse 19 affirms that the wicked who turn from their evil ways and do what is lawful and right will live, emphasizing God's mercy.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33:20, how will the Lord judge the house of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: According to their ways
questions.explanation: Verse 20 says the Lord will judge the house of Israel every one after his ways, highlighting personal responsibility.

questions.question: What significant event is reported in Ezekiel 33:21?
options: One who escaped Jerusalem reported the city was smitten
questions.correctAnswer: One who escaped Jerusalem reported the city was smitten
questions.explanation: Verse 21 records that in the twelfth year of captivity, a survivor came to Ezekiel and said that Jerusalem was smitten, signaling the city's fall.

questions.question: What change occurred to Ezekiel before the survivor from Jerusalem arrived, according to Ezekiel 33:22?
options: His mouth was opened and he was no longer dumb
He was taken to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: His mouth was opened and he was no longer dumb
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains that the hand of the Lord was upon Ezekiel, opening his mouth and removing his silence before the survivor arrived.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 33:12–13 teach about the importance of humility and ongoing obedience?
options: Past righteousness guarantees eternal life regardless of current actions
One's own righteousness can save if trusted fully
Righteousness does not save if one sins afterward, emphasizing humility and obedience
Obedience is optional for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness does not save if one sins afterward, emphasizing humility and obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 teach that the righteousness of the righteous won't save him if he sins afterward, underscoring the need for ongoing humility and obedience rather than self-trusting.

questions.question: What practical lesson about repentance and restoration can be drawn from Ezekiel 33:14–16?
options: Restoring what was lost and living rightly leads to life and forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Restoring what was lost and living rightly leads to life and forgiveness
questions.explanation: Verses 14 to 16 show that if the wicked turn from sin, restore what was taken, and walk in the statutes without sin, they shall live and their sins will not be held against them.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 33:17–20 reveals that God's judgment is fair and based on each person's ways.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 17 through 20 address the claim that God's way is unequal but affirm that God will judge each person according to their own ways, demonstrating divine fairness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 33:18, a righteous person can sin without consequence because of their previous righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 18 clearly states that when the righteous turn from righteousness and commit iniquity, they will die, indicating that previous righteousness does not exempt one from consequences.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 33 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 33.

questions.question: What accusation do the inhabitants of the wastes of the land of Israel make regarding the inheritance of the land?
options: Abraham was only one and inherited the land, but we are many and the land is given to us
The land belongs only to the priests and Levites
The land was never promised to Abraham
The land is cursed and should be abandoned
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham was only one and inherited the land, but we are many and the land is given to us
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Ezekiel 33:24, where the people claim that Abraham was one and inherited the land, but they are many and the land belongs to them.

questions.question: What sinful actions does God accuse the people of in Ezekiel 33:25?
options: Eating with the blood, lifting eyes toward idols, and shedding blood
Building altars to the true God
questions.correctAnswer: Eating with the blood, lifting eyes toward idols, and shedding blood
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:25 explicitly lists these sins as reasons why they should not expect to possess the land.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33:26, what additional sins do the people commit besides idolatry and bloodshed?
options: Standing on their sword, working abominations, and defiling neighbors' wives
Breaking the Sabbath and neglecting offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Standing on their sword, working abominations, and defiling neighbors' wives
questions.explanation: The verse Ezekiel 33:26 accuses them of these specific sins, highlighting their moral corruption.

questions.question: What fate does God declare for those in the wastes, open fields, forts, and caves in Ezekiel 33:27?
options: They shall fall by the sword, be devoured by beasts, or die of pestilence
They shall be taken captive and exiled
They shall be protected and prosper
They shall build new cities and live peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall by the sword, be devoured by beasts, or die of pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:27 clearly states that those in various places will face violent death or pestilence as judgment.

questions.question: What will happen to the land and its strength according to Ezekiel 33:28?
options: It will be laid most desolate and the pomp of her strength shall cease
It will be restored and flourish again
It will be divided among the nations
It will become a land of milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: It will be laid most desolate and the pomp of her strength shall cease
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:28 declares that the land and its strength will be desolate, emphasizing the severity of God's judgment.

questions.question: What realization will the people come to after the land is laid desolate due to their abominations?
options: They shall know that I am the LORD
They will migrate to other lands
questions.correctAnswer: They shall know that I am the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:29 states that the desolation will lead to the recognition of God's sovereignty.

questions.question: How do the children of Israel behave towards Ezekiel's prophetic words as described in Ezekiel 33:31?
options: They hear his words but do not do them, showing love with their mouth but their hearts go after covetousness
They reject his words and persecute him
questions.correctAnswer: They hear his words but do not do them, showing love with their mouth but their hearts go after covetousness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:31 describes the people's superficial reception of the message without true obedience.

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by Ezekiel being compared to 'a very lovely song' that they hear but do not do in Ezekiel 33:32?
options: Simile illustrating the people's superficial appreciation
questions.correctAnswer: Simile illustrating the people's superficial appreciation
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:32 uses a simile comparing Ezekiel to a lovely song, highlighting that the people enjoy hearing but fail to act on the message.

questions.question: What event is reported to Ezekiel in Ezekiel 33:21, marking a turning point in the chapter?
options: An escaped one from Jerusalem reports that the city is smitten
A great feast is held in the city
questions.correctAnswer: An escaped one from Jerusalem reports that the city is smitten
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:21 records the arrival of a fugitive who confirms the city's destruction, a pivotal moment in the narrative.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'my mouth was opened, and I was no more dumb' in Ezekiel 33:22?
options: It signifies God enabling Ezekiel to prophesy effectively after the news from Jerusalem
It means Ezekiel was healed from a physical ailment
It indicates Ezekiel was silent before this moment
It suggests Ezekiel could now speak foreign languages
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God enabling Ezekiel to prophesy effectively after the news from Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:22 shows that God's hand empowered Ezekiel to speak boldly following the critical news, marking a renewed prophetic mission.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage has a similar theme of a watchman warning the people to turn from their wicked ways as found in Ezekiel 33:7-9?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 62:6-7
questions.explanation: Isaiah 62:6-7 also depicts watchmen appointed on the walls of Jerusalem to warn the people, paralleling Ezekiel's watchman imagery (Ezekiel 33:7-9).

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'watchman' in Ezekiel 33:2-7 carries the connotation of both protector and one who warns of danger?
questions.correctAnswer: Tsômêr
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Tsômêr' (צֹפֶר) means 'watchman' or 'sentinel' tasked with vigilance and warning, as used in Ezekiel 33:2-7.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 33:11, God expresses a desire concerning the wicked. What is this desire?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:11 states that God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked but desires that they turn from their ways and live.

questions.question: Does Ezekiel 33:13 teach that a righteous person's past righteousness will save him if he later sins?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:13 teaches that if a righteous person trusts in his past righteousness but commits iniquity, he will die for his iniquity; past righteousness does not save him.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of warning the wicked and God's desire for repentance found in Ezekiel 33:8-11?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Peter 3:9
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:9 echoes God's patience and desire that none should perish but all come to repentance, paralleling Ezekiel 33:8-11.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 33 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 33 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What responsibility is given to the watchman according to Ezekiel 33:2-3?
options: To warn the people when the sword comes upon the land
To lead the people into battle
To judge the people according to their deeds
To store food and supplies for the community
questions.correctAnswer: To warn the people when the sword comes upon the land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:2-3 teaches that the watchman’s role is to blow the trumpet to warn the people when he sees the sword coming upon the land, signifying impending danger and judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33:4-5, who bears responsibility if a person hears the trumpet but does not take warning?
questions.correctAnswer: The person himself
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:4-5 explains that if a person hears the warning trumpet but does not take warning, his blood is upon his own head, meaning he bears the responsibility for his death.

questions.question: What consequence does the watchman face if he sees the sword coming but fails to warn the people, as stated in Ezekiel 33:6?
options: God will require the blood of the person taken at the watchman’s hand
The watchman will be rewarded for silence
The watchman will be made king
questions.correctAnswer: God will require the blood of the person taken at the watchman’s hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:6 teaches that if the watchman does not warn the people, and someone dies, God will hold the watchman responsible for that person's blood, emphasizing the seriousness of prophetic duty.

questions.question: Ezekiel 33:7 declares the prophet Ezekiel as what to the house of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: A watchman
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:7 explicitly states that Ezekiel is set as a watchman to the house of Israel, tasked with hearing God's word and warning the people.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 33:11 reveal about God's attitude toward the death of the wicked?
options: God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked
God delights in punishing the wicked
God predestines the wicked to die
questions.correctAnswer: God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:11 shows God's merciful attribute, stating He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked but desires their repentance and life.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the combined message of Ezekiel 33:12-13 regarding righteousness and iniquity?
options: Righteousness does not guarantee life if one sins, and wickedness does not guarantee death if one repents
Righteousness always guarantees eternal life regardless of actions
Sin has no consequences for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness does not guarantee life if one sins, and wickedness does not guarantee death if one repents
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:12-13 teaches the doctrine of individual responsibility and repentance: the righteous can die if they sin and the wicked can live if they turn from their wickedness, emphasizing the dynamic nature of divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 33:15-16, what happens to the sins of the wicked who repent and do what is lawful and right?
options: Their sins are not mentioned to them, and they shall surely live
Their sins are forgiven only after death
questions.correctAnswer: Their sins are not mentioned to them, and they shall surely live
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:15-16 reveals the doctrine of forgiveness and restoration: once the wicked fully repent and live righteously, their previous sins are no longer mentioned, and they are granted life.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 33:17-20 address about the people's perception of God's justice?
options: They claim God's way is not equal, but God will judge each according to their ways
They think God's laws are too strict
questions.correctAnswer: They claim God's way is not equal, but God will judge each according to their ways
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:17-20 deals with the people's complaint that God's way is unequal, but God responds that He will judge each person fairly according to their deeds, affirming His perfect justice.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 33:21-22 narrate the moment of prophetic restoration for Ezekiel?
options: Ezekiel's mouth was opened and he was no longer dumb when the news of Jerusalem's fall arrived
Ezekiel was struck dumb and could not speak
Ezekiel received a new vision of hope
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel's mouth was opened and he was no longer dumb when the news of Jerusalem's fall arrived
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:21-22 describes that before the escaped messenger came, God's hand was upon Ezekiel, opening his mouth so he could speak the word of the LORD, signifying renewed prophetic authority.

questions.question: What accusation do the inhabitants of the wastes make in Ezekiel 33:24, and what does this reveal about human nature in rebellion?
options: They claim the land belongs to them because they are many, showing pride and entitlement
They admit their sin and seek forgiveness
They blame God for their exile
They desire to return to Jerusalem peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: They claim the land belongs to them because they are many, showing pride and entitlement
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:24 reveals the rebellious attitude of the exiles who arrogantly claim inheritance by number, reflecting human pride and rejection of divine justice.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's judgment described in Ezekiel 33:27-29?
options: God's holiness and justice in purging abominations
God's favoritism towards Israel regardless of sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and justice in purging abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:27-29 shows God's holiness and justice as He declares the land will be made desolate because of the people's abominations, highlighting that sin must be punished to maintain divine purity.

questions.question: What contradictory behavior do the people exhibit towards Ezekiel in Ezekiel 33:30-32?
options: They listen attentively but do not obey, showing superficial love but inward covetousness
They fully obey all his words
They seek to replace him with another prophet
questions.correctAnswer: They listen attentively but do not obey, showing superficial love but inward covetousness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:30-32 describes how the people gather to hear Ezekiel's words but do not practice them, revealing hypocrisy and a heart turned toward covetousness despite outward appearances.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ezekiel 33:8-9 and 33:11 convey about the prophet’s role and God's desire for sinners?
options: The prophet must warn sinners to turn or face death, but God desires that the wicked turn and live
The prophet can ignore the wicked's sin without consequences
God desires the death of all sinners without warning
The prophet’s warnings have no effect on the sinner’s fate
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet must warn sinners to turn or face death, but God desires that the wicked turn and live
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:8-9 and 33:11 together teach that the prophet has the responsibility to warn the wicked, and while the wicked may die in sin if they refuse, God desires repentance and life, emphasizing divine mercy and prophetic duty.

questions.question: What theological truth is synthesized from Ezekiel 33:14-16 about repentance and restoration?
options: Repentance leads to full restoration where previous sins are forgotten and life is assured
Past sins always condemn the repentant
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance leads to full restoration where previous sins are forgotten and life is assured
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:14-16 teaches that if the wicked turn from sin and do what is right, their past sins are not mentioned and they shall live, illustrating the doctrine of forgiveness and renewal.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is unjust because the wicked sometimes prosper and the righteous suffer. What does Ezekiel 33:12-20 teach about God's justice?
options: God judges each person according to their ways, and righteousness or wickedness only affect life when paired with corresponding behavior
God ignores human behavior in judgment
God punishes everyone equally regardless of their deeds
questions.correctAnswer: God judges each person according to their ways, and righteousness or wickedness only affect life when paired with corresponding behavior
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 33:12-20 clarifies that God's justice is perfect and individual: the righteous must continue in righteousness to live, and the wicked can live if they repent, affirming that God judges fairly contrary to sceptical claims.
